item.title: Structured Data Needs Verified Facts, Not Guesses
item.description: Structured data only helps when the facts are verified. Before adding schema, confirm domains, locations, social profiles, service pages, and form behavior.

item.title: The Website Link Is Not the GitHub Repo
item.description: A private GitHub repository, a local preview, and a public website URL are three different things. Keeping those links straight prevents launch confusion.

item.title: Authority Pages Beat Competitor Copying
item.description: Competitor research should not turn into copying. The better move is building authority pages that answer more buyer questions than the competitor ever did.

item.title: Operational History Beats Generic About Pages
item.description: Most About pages are too vague. A stronger company history section turns real milestones, operational depth, and capacity into trust.

item.title: Removing Outdated Website Claims Takes More Than One Search
item.description: When a website needs outdated claims removed, do not only edit the visible paragraph. Search components, metadata, generated pages, and built output before calling it done.

item.title: AI Website Edits Need Change Boundaries
item.description: When using AI to edit a website, the most important part of the prompt is often the boundary: what should change, what should stay untouched, and how to verify the result.

item.title: Process Photos Beat People Photos When Buyers Need Proof
item.description: Buyer-focused websites should use photos that prove capability. For technical businesses, process photos often build more trust than generic people photos.

item.title: Hero Sections Should Earn the Scroll
item.description: A homepage hero should do more than look good. It should make the offer obvious, show proof, guide the next click, and transition cleanly into the page.

item.title: Location Sections Should Sell Capacity
item.description: A location section should do more than list addresses. Use it to explain reach, capacity, trust, and the next step a buyer should take.

item.title: Manufacturing Websites Need Specs, Not Slogans
item.description: Manufacturing websites often hide the details buyers and AI systems need. Specs, materials, tolerances, examples, and quote workflows beat vague marketing copy.

item.title: Proof Blocks Beat Generic Stats
item.description: Website stats work better when they explain why a buyer should care. Turn simple numbers into proof blocks that connect experience, capacity, process, and fit.

item.title: The Website Rebuild Step That Saves the Whole Project
item.description: Before rebuilding a business website, inventory the current pages, images, content, and conversion paths. It prevents redesigns from losing useful assets and search value.
